briefing:
EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
A significant development is the reported "historic agreement" for the full disarmament of Hamas in Gaza, though immediate contradictions from Hamas and Israeli reservations indicate a complex and uncertain implementation phase. Concurrently, escalating tensions in the wider Middle East continue, marked by Iranian drone attacks on US bases in Kuwait and Bahrain, retaliatory US/Saudi strikes in Iran and Iraq, and Israel's destruction of Hezbollah tunnels in southern Lebanon following a ceasefire violation.

IRAN
Iran's military has launched drone attacks on US bases in the Gulf, including Ahmad al-Jaber and Ali Al-Salem in Kuwait, and Sheikh Isa in Bahrain, claiming to have struck fighter jet shelters, satellite communication systems, and equipment depots. Kuwaiti authorities reported one fatality from an Iranian attack on a Chinese commercial building. Iran's IRGC also claimed to have destroyed three US F-35 fighter jets and damaged three others at Muwaffaq Salti Air Base in Jordan, a claim explicitly denied by US CENTCOM, which stated all missiles and drones were intercepted or missed targets.

In response to US actions, Iran has accused the US of targeting residential areas on Qeshm Island, Minab, and Zanjan, resulting in the deaths of three IRGC members (Mahmoud Molajabari, Mohammad Reza Cheraghi, Jamal Amiri) in Zanjan and a two-year-old child in Qeshm, as well as damage to student dormitories in Ahvaz and a sports hall in Fars. Iran also stated that US forces targeted anti-ship cruise missile launchers near Bandar Abbas. Iran's Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Qalibaf condemned the US strikes, vowing retaliation. Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi warned of potential Israeli "false-flag" operations in the region after a drone attack in Egypt and secured assurances from Cyprus that foreign bases on its territory would not be used against Iran.

Economic reports indicate fluctuating oil prices, with Brent crude down but still on track for a monthly growth near 20%. The war is reported to have increased profits for major oil companies. China denied a Reuters report about a planned shipment of 400 Chinese-made shoulder-fired air defense missiles to Iran. The US Treasury Department imposed new sanctions on one individual and five companies linked to Iran's Mahan Air.

ISRAEL
The Israel Defense Forces (IDF) have conducted operations in Gaza, destroying four Hamas weapon depots containing rifles, explosive devices, anti-tank missile launchers, and ammunition. In southern Lebanon, the IDF demolished Hezbollah's extensive tunnel system under the Beaufort Ridge using approximately 700 tons of explosives. This action was announced as a direct response to Hezbollah's violation of the ceasefire agreement yesterday, when it targeted an unmanned bulldozer with an explosive drone. Residents of the Upper Galilee were warned of a large blast and advised to open windows. The IDF continues to monitor the Ali Taher ridge where dozens of Hezbollah operatives are believed to be holed up, and has carried out artillery strikes in Talouse, Halta, Shema, Shaihin, and a drone strike in Nabatiyeh.

In the West Bank, Israeli settlers illegally entered the outskirts of Nablus (Area A), reportedly vandalizing a cemetery and clashing with Palestinians who threw stones. An Israeli civilian fired into the air, with no reported injuries. IDF forces were deployed to remove the settlers and reiterated that entry into Area A is prohibited and dangerous. Two Israeli settlement activists illegally crossed into Syria from the Mount Hermon area, were located by IDF troops, returned, and detained. IDF operations in Beit Ommar resulted in the arrest of wanted individuals and the discovery of weapons, and in Tubas, ten pipe bombs were found and destroyed.

Defense Minister Israel Katz held a security assessment, ordering high readiness for IDF forces. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu returned from his US visit, landing at Nevatim air base due to security concerns. A "mutiny" by dozens of Givati Brigade soldiers at the Sde Teiman base was reported, triggered by the removal of traditional platoon signs by their commander.

GAZA & WEST BANK
US President Donald Trump announced that the "Peace Council" has reached a "historic agreement" for the "complete disarmament of Hamas and all armed groups in Gaza." The agreement, reportedly brokered by Egypt, Qatar, and Turkey, outlines a phased approach where Hamas formally commits to disarmament, relinquishes all civil and security governance roles, and transfers weapon control to a new technocrat Palestinian government. Israeli forces would gradually withdraw as disarmament is completed, overseen by an international stabilization force and a new Palestinian police force. The process is expected to last 6-8 months (N12) or 200-250 days (VahidOnline).

However, senior Hamas official Ghazi Hamad stated that Hamas would not disarm before a full Israeli withdrawal from Gaza and insisted weapons would be transferred to the "National Committee for Gaza Management" without Israeli involvement, contradicting aspects of the US announcement. The Palestinian Islamic Jihad movement expressed reservations about the announced agreement. A US official claimed Iran attempted to persuade Hamas to delay signing the agreement, but Hamas proceeded. A signing ceremony for the second phase of the ceasefire is anticipated in Cairo next week.

In military operations, the IDF destroyed four Hamas weapon depots across Gaza. The IDF's 188th Brigade completed an eight-month mission in southern Gaza, destroying over ten Hamas tunnels, including one used for holding hostages. Palestinian media reported one fatality and several injuries from an Israeli drone strike in Jabalia.

In the West Bank, dozens of Israeli settlers entered the outskirts of Nablus, an unapproved and dangerous activity in Area A, where they reportedly vandalized a cemetery and clashed with Palestinians. An Israeli civilian fired shots into the air. IDF forces intervened to remove the settlers. An operation in Beit Ommar by IDF, Shin Bet, and Border Police scanned over 170 locations, arrested wanted individuals, and found various weapons. In Tubas, IDF forces located and destroyed ten pipe bombs. An incident in Shomron saw an assailant accelerate a vehicle towards IDF troops, who responded with fire, neutralizing the individual without Israeli casualties.

LEBANON
The IDF announced the destruction of "several key underground routes" of Hezbollah's tunnel system beneath the Beaufort Ridge in southern Lebanon. This action involved approximately 700 tons of explosives and was stated as a response to Hezbollah's violation of the ceasefire agreement, specifically targeting an unmanned bulldozer with an explosive drone. Israeli military officials stated that the tunnels were part of Hezbollah's "Bader" unit's invasion plan for Galilee settlements. Residents of the Upper Galilee were warned to open windows to prevent damage from the expected large blast.

Artillery fire was reported from the IDF towards the villages of Talouse, Halta, Shema, and Shaihin in southern Lebanon. A drone attack was also reported in Nabatiyeh. The IDF continues to operate in the Ali Taher ridge area and maintains high readiness, stating that any harm to its forces will be met with a response. Images from Lebanese sources showed snow-like dust covering southern Lebanese villages following violent Israeli explosions.

SYRIA & IRAQ
Two Israeli settlement activists illegally crossed the border into Syria from the Mount Hermon area; they were located by IDF troops, returned to Israeli territory, and detained.

In Iraq, Iranian-Kurdish opposition camps in Erbil, Sulaymaniyah, and Duhok provinces were targeted by Iranian suicide drones. Press TV reported massive strikes on these camps, stating they belong to "separatist terrorist organizations." The Iraqi government rejected US-Saudi claims that recent drone attacks on Saudi Arabia originated from Iraqi territory, stating it had no prior information or approval for such attacks. Five IRGC members, described as "advisors," killed in earlier US-Saudi strikes in Iraq, were repatriated. Syrian President Ahmed Shar'a expressed support for Saudi Arabia's security and stability.

GULF STATES
Saudi Arabia is reportedly preparing for a large-scale military operation against Houthi forces in Yemen, potentially involving sea and ground attacks in the central al-Bayda province. The objective is to break the Houthi blockade on Saudi oil exports through the southern Red Sea. Saudi Arabia, along with 14 other nations (including Turkey, Pakistan, Egypt, Sudan, and Djibouti), announced support for forming a multinational maritime coalition to secure shipping lanes in the Red Sea, Gulf of Aden, and Bab al-Mandab Strait, with its headquarters expected in Saudi Arabia. Reports also indicated Saudi airstrikes on Houthi-controlled Sanaa.

Iran launched drone attacks on US military assets in Kuwait and Bahrain. The Iranian Army announced that its "suicide drones" struck fighter jet shelters, satellite communication systems, and equipment depots at Kuwait's Ahmad al-Jaber Air Base. Earlier, Iran's IRGC claimed to have destroyed two drone hangars and a fuel storage facility at the US Ali Al Salem Air Base in Kuwait and struck the Sheikh Isa Air Base in Bahrain with "Arash drones." Satellite imagery reportedly shows new damage at Ali Al-Salem Air Base. Kuwaiti authorities reported one fatality following an Iranian attack on a Chinese commercial building. US officials stated that the Pentagon is reconsidering the scope of its military presence in Kuwait in response to Iranian attacks, citing Kuwaiti officials' discontent with the US initiating a war without consulting them.

Pakistan reportedly secured Iran's cooperation to safely escort a Qatari LNG shipment through the Strait of Hormuz, easing its energy shortages. The UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham offered to assist Oman in a military mission to reopen the Strait of Hormuz after a ceasefire, an offer Iran previously warned against regarding Western intervention. US CENTCOM denied Iranian claims that an Iranian cargo ship, M/T Nora, had broken a US blockade in the Strait of Hormuz, stating that the "steel wall" blockade with 20 warships, hundreds of aircraft, and thousands of troops remains fully enforced.

KEY DEVELOPMENTS
1.  **Gaza Disarmament Agreement**: US President Trump announced a "historic agreement" for the full disarmament of Hamas, to be implemented over 6-8 months, with a new technocrat Palestinian government taking control, pending Israeli withdrawal. Hamas senior official Ghazi Hamad contradicted key aspects, stating no disarmament would occur before full Israeli withdrawal.
2.  **Beaufort Ridge Tunnels Demolished**: The IDF destroyed Hezbollah's extensive tunnel network under the Beaufort Ridge in southern Lebanon using 700 tons of explosives, in retaliation for a Hezbollah ceasefire violation.
3.  **Iranian Strikes on US Bases**: Iran launched drone attacks on US military bases in Kuwait (Ahmad al-Jaber, Ali Al-Salem) and Bahrain (Sheikh Isa), claiming to strike critical facilities. Kuwait reported one fatality.
4.  **US/Saudi Strikes in Iran and Iraq**: US/Saudi strikes in Iran targeted Qeshm, Minab, and Zanjan, killing three IRGC members and a two-year-old child. In Iraq, five IRGC members were killed in US-Saudi strikes, and Iran launched drone attacks on Iranian-Kurdish opposition camps in Erbil, Sulaymaniyah, and Duhok.
5.  **Saudi Maritime Coalition & Yemen Offensive**: Saudi Arabia announced the formation of a multinational maritime coalition in the Red Sea and Gulf of Aden and is reportedly preparing a large-scale military offensive against Houthis in Yemen.
6.  **West Bank Settler Incidents**: Israeli settlers illegally entered Area A near Nablus, vandalized a cemetery, and clashed with Palestinians. Two Israeli settlement activists illegally crossed into Syria.
7.  **Givati Brigade "Mutiny"**: Dozens of Givati Brigade soldiers reportedly left their base at Sde Teiman without authorization after commanders removed traditional platoon signs, prompting an IDF investigation.

THREAT ASSESSMENT
The risk of escalation remains extremely high across multiple fronts. **Active flashpoints** include the ongoing strikes and counter-strikes between Iran and the US/Israel in the Gulf region, with US military presence in Kuwait being reconsidered. The **Gaza Strip** is a critical flashpoint as the proposed disarmament deal faces immediate contradictions from Hamas and Israeli skepticism, creating uncertainty regarding its implementation and potential for renewed conflict. **Southern Lebanon** is highly volatile following Israel's major demolition of Hezbollah tunnels in response to a ceasefire violation, with both sides maintaining high alert. **The West Bank** continues to see settler incursions into Palestinian areas and clashes, indicating sustained friction and potential for wider unrest. **Yemen** faces the imminent threat of a large-scale Saudi military offensive against Houthi forces, potentially opening a new significant theater of conflict.

**Military posture changes** include the IDF's sustained high readiness, Saudi Arabia's preparations for a substantial offensive in Yemen, and the US considering a reduction of its military footprint in Kuwait. **Red lines** appear to be the complete disarmament of Hamas for Israel before any full withdrawal from Gaza, and for Iran, any continued US aggression against its territory or proxies will be met with retaliation. The threat of drone attacks against Israeli public gatherings is a significant new concern for Israeli security officials.

REGIONAL & INTERNATIONAL RESPONSE
The **US** response is multifaceted: President Trump announced the Gaza disarmament deal, while the Treasury Department imposed new sanctions on entities linked to Iran's Mahan Air. US intelligence is reportedly aiding Ukraine's deep-strike drone campaigns into Russia. Reports indicate Trump's frustration with the protracted conflict with Iran and a growing public opposition to the war. The US is considering reducing its military presence in Kuwait in response to Iranian attacks.
**Gulf states** are reacting to the regional instability, with Saudi Arabia leading the formation of a multinational maritime coalition and preparing for a major offensive in Yemen. Kuwaiti officials have expressed unhappiness with the US initiating a war without their consultation. Qatar is a key mediator in the Gaza peace talks. The Sultan of Oman has been approached by the UK regarding potential involvement in reopening the Strait of Hormuz.
**European Union members** show concern over migration, with France strengthening border controls with Spain and Italy considering suspending the Schengen agreement with Spain due to the migrant influx into Ceuta. Cyprus has assured Iran its territory will not be used for hostile acts. UEFA has voted to boycott FIFA World Cup competitions in protest of FIFA's commercial plans.
**Russia** has claimed to intercept a large number of Ukrainian drones, struck a military shipment near Odesa, and targeted a US-owned drone factory in Kyiv. Russia has also designated the owner of Telegram as a "terrorist" for refusing surveillance demands.
**China** has explicitly dismissed reports from Reuters concerning a planned shipment of 400 MANPADS to Iran as "not true and not factual at all."
**Turkey** is a mediator in the Gaza disarmament talks. President Erdogan reportedly advised Lebanese President Aoun against rushing into an agreement with Israel.
**Pakistan** has been mediating between Iran and the US and reportedly secured Iran's cooperation to allow a Qatari LNG shipment to pass safely through the Strait of Hormuz.
The **UN** has warned about the human consequences of escalating tensions in the Middle East.

INTELLIGENCE NOTES
Significant contradictions persist in reporting. Iran's claims of destroying US F-35s and other aircraft at Jordan's Muwaffaq Salti Air Base are directly refuted by US CENTCOM, which asserts no US aircraft were damaged. Similarly, CENTCOM denies Iranian claims that the cargo ship M/T Nora broke a US blockade in the Strait of Hormuz. The "historic agreement" on Gaza disarmament, announced by Trump, is immediately complicated by a senior Hamas official, Ghazi Hamad, who insists disarmament will not occur before a full Israeli withdrawal, a different sequencing than presented by the US. The Chinese Foreign Ministry also directly denies the Reuters report about an impending shipment of 400 MANPADS to Iran. The Iraqi government has denied any prior knowledge or approval of US-Saudi strikes on its territory. The Egyptian Minister of Information denied a Wall Street Journal report claiming Egypt blames Iran for a recent drone attack in Damietta.

Unverified claims include reports of 6 missiles launched from Khomein, sightings of a drone in the Hamedan sky, and Israeli Channel 14's cryptic warning of a repeat of "March 9th in Tehran." There are also unconfirmed reports from Israeli sources that Trump is "angry" and planning a "dangerous order" or that US attacks against Iran will continue tonight. The circumstances surrounding the Qeshm casualties are subject to differing narratives, with some suggesting the targeted residential home was used by "Arzeshi" (pro-regime) individuals for military purposes, blaming the Iranian regime for placing launchers in residential areas.

Propaganda indicators are evident in the language used by some sources. Press TV consistently frames US and Israeli actions as "aggression" and "terrorist," while portraying Iranian responses as "retaliatory" and its casualties as "martyrs." Its reports often make unsubstantiated claims of extensive US military losses. CENTCOM has explicitly engaged in information warfare by issuing statements directly debunking IRGC claims. Iranian political figures, such as Qalibaf, use strong, confrontational rhetoric against the US.

Reporting gaps include a lack of precise details on the number and status of Givati soldiers involved in the "mutiny" at Sde Teiman, the specific nature and impact of alleged Iranian-linked cyberattacks on Minnesota water treatment plants, and comprehensive damage assessments for all Iranian facilities reportedly targeted by US/Saudi strikes. The full text and universally accepted details of the Gaza disarmament agreement remain elusive.
